event_name: Start of US and Israeli military action against Iran; tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz largely stops
capacity_note: EIA estimate (April 2026 STEO press release): Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, UAE, Qatar and Bahrain collectively shut in 7.5 million b/d of crude production in March 2026. IEA: flows through the strait fell from about 20 million b/d to an average of 2.7 million b/d in March, April and May. Production shut-ins and strait flows are different measures.
notes: Feb 28, 2026 was a Saturday; day zero is the next trading day. AP (via Michigan Public, May 8, 2026) also gives Feb. 28: https://www.michiganpublic.org/2026-05-08/the-u-s-fires-on-iranian-tankers-trying-to-evade-its-blockade-amid-a-hormuz-standoff . IEA strait flow figures: https://www.iea.org/commentaries/how-global-oil-supplies-have-readjusted-to-help-fill-the-huge-gap-left-by-the-strait-of-hormuz-shock (the IEA page returned 403 on Oct 7; the figures were matched in a Hellenic Shipping News reprint dated June 29, 2026, marked Source: IEA). The 7.5 million b/d figure is from EIA press586, not EIA article 67424. Source check Oct 7, 2026: docs/checks/source_check_war_rows_2026-10-07.md.

event_name: Iran's Revolutionary Guards state the Strait of Hormuz is closed; major shipping lines suspend transits
capacity_note: No separate volume; part of the W01 disruption.
notes: AFP (Mar 1): the Revolutionary Guards declared the strait closed on Saturday (Feb 28, the alt date), and Maersk suspended all crossings (Mar 1, the event date). Caixin lists the declaration under 'late Saturday, March 1' and the Hapag-Lloyd suspension under 'Sunday, March 2', but March 1, 2026 was a Sunday, so its weekday labels are off by one day; the first draft's March 2 came from Caixin. Day zero is Monday March 2 under any of these dates. Wikipedia (pointer) cites March 2. Source check Oct 7, 2026: docs/checks/source_check_war_rows_2026-10-07.md.

event_name: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation declares force majeure and cuts crude output
capacity_note: KPC did not say how much it would cut. Kuwait produced about 2.6 million b/d of crude in February.

notes: Location is approximate (central Kuwait), for the map only.

event_name: Saudi Arabia cuts crude output by about 2 million b/d to about 8 million b/d (Safaniya and Zuluf offshore fields shut)
capacity_note: Reuters, two sources: output cut by about 2 million b/d to around 8 million b/d after the two fields were shut. Some exports diverted to Yanbu on the Red Sea.
notes: E17 uses March 13, the date of the Reuters report; the report gives no date for the cut itself. A Bloomberg video dated March 9 says Saudi Arabia began output cuts as storage filled: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-03-09/saudi-arabia-begins-oil-output-cuts-as-storage-fills-up-video (returned 403 on Oct 7, so the alt date is unconfirmed). EIA 67424 supports only the general statement that Saudi Arabia shut in production, not the figures. Starter row's cause was 'attack'; changed to 'blockade' because Reuters attributes the cut to the closed strait and reports more oil routed to Yanbu to avoid it. Source check Oct 7, 2026: docs/checks/source_check_war_rows_2026-10-07.md.

Reported price moves differ: Maritime Executive says WTI fell 14% and Brent 11%; All India Radio says more than 11%. event_name: US and Iran sign the Islamabad memorandum to end hostilities and reopen the strait
capacity_note: A supply-returning event. Reported terms (Arab News Pakistan) include reopening the strait, waiving US sanctions on Iranian oil and lifting the US naval blockade.
notes: EIA pages disagree by a day: EIA 68245 says 'the June 17 Memorandum of Understanding', press590 says 'the June 18 memorandum of understanding' (E19 note). 'Islamabad MoU' is the name used by Pakistan's prime minister in Arab News Pakistan (an outlet, not an agency): https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2647648 . The first draft's 'temporarily' and 'signed digitally' were not in any source and were removed. Source check Oct 7, 2026: docs/checks/source_check_war_rows_2026-10-07.md.
